methodology.absolute_summary: median, Type-7 quartiles, IQR, min/max; no outlier removal

methodology.aggregation: median of per-block aggregate throughput, with P5/P95 and retained min/max across the same blocks
methodology.cross_thread_backpressure: bounded per-worker mailbox; a producer facing a full mailbox frees the block itself rather than blocking, and the fallback count is published
methodology.operation_stream: versioned splitmix64-v1 deterministic operation streams; the two distribution workloads use separate lifetime and requested-size streams, normal allocation alignment, eight live slots per worker, and page touching; existing workloads retain their prior stream; live bytes at RSS peak and actual peak live requested bytes come from a separate instrumented replay so telemetry does not contaminate timed throughput or published peak RSS
methodology.oversubscription: thread points are literal worker counts 1/2/3/4/6/8; points above the allowed logical CPU count are labeled oversubscribed and describe contention, not core scaling
methodology.pairing: all five allocators run the same frozen per-worker operation count and the same stream inside one block, in a rotated near-balanced order
methodology.percentile_method: empirical P5/P50/P95 over paired per-run observations; linear interpolation h=(n-1)p; bands are not confidence intervals
methodology.rigor: mixed rigor - 3-block legacy coverage plus 40-repetition distribution bands
methodology.seed_chain: splitmix64-v1 chain over (master seed, workload tag, worker-count cell, repetition/block, worker index); allocator identity, time and scheduling are absent; distribution size streams derive from the worker seed with the size-v1 domain
methodology.statistics_omitted: no bootstrap confidence intervals and no noise gating; legacy workloads remain three-block coverage signals, while distribution workloads use at least 40 repetitions for empirical percentile bands
methodology.work_normalization: operations per worker are calibrated once per (pattern, thread point) against upstream-mimalloc and frozen across allocators; total work scales with worker count

patterns.description: 16-64 B small-object hot path, high alloc/free rate, small live set
8 B-4 KiB log-uniform general mix including realloc, medium live set
64 KiB-4 MiB buffers with one-byte-per-page touching
16-512 B producer/consumer handoff; blocks freed by another worker
Larson & Krishnan server workload: 8-1000 B random slot replacement over a 5000-block array per thread; arrays rotate between threads each round, so later frees are remote
xmalloc-test (Lever & Boreham): dedicated producer threads allocate 8-128 B blocks and hand them to dedicated consumer threads that free them
normal allocations with requested sizes uniformly selected from exact powers 2^16 through 2^22; eight live slots per worker, page-touched
normal allocations with unbiased uniform integer requested sizes from 64 KiB through 4 MiB; eight live slots per worker, page-touched
unbiased uniform requested sizes from 96 KiB through 512 KiB on long-lived workers; eight live slots per worker, page-touched
the large-class-persistent stream, run by each worker as 8 short-lived threads that exit still owning live blocks, which the next thread frees

scaling.rigor_label: mixed rigor - 3-block legacy coverage plus 40-repetition distribution bands

sampling.method: polled externally from child spawn through process exit, so startup, setup, warmup, measured work, and teardown are all in scope; the process-lifetime peak is retained and phase durations are recorded separately
sampling.source: external /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup Rss, parsed as integer kB * 1024

sampling.peak_source: external /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup Rss polled from child spawn through exit, the same peak the sweep publishes
sampling.post_drain_source: the child's own /proc/self/statm resident pages x page size, read in-process after every worker thread was joined, at fixed offsets from that instant
sampling.release_definition: per run, the first post-drain offset whose RSS is within release_tolerance_bytes of the last sample's (perf-ab's definition); P50/P95 across runs
